judgement.headline: The message uses a classic fake-check overpayment scheme with a non-existent company name and a free email domain.
judgement.assessment: The message exhibits multiple high-severity risk signals: it describes a fake-check/overpayment pattern where a $3,200 cheque is sent and the recipient is asked to forward $1,400 via Zelle, a hard-to-reverse method [F1][F2]. The sender uses a personal outlook.com address while claiming to represent a design studio [F3]. No web source confirms the existence of 'Quillmere Design Studio' as a real company; similarly named entities (Quill Creative Studio, Quill Design Studio, Quill Fine Art Creations) appear in sources [S2][S3][S5][S6], but 'Quillmere' appears only as a sample project name 'Quillmere Cat Sitting' [S1]. Claim checks for the company, the recruiter's role, and the payment details are all inconclusive [C1][C2][C3][C4]. The named recruiter, David Laurent, appears in public profiles as an exteriors color specialist, a set designer/photographer in Luxembourg, a recruiter in Arkansas, and a musician — none matching a project manager at Quillmere Design Studio [S17][S18][S19][S20][S21]. Recruitment fraud advisories describe this exact overpayment-and-forward scheme as a known scam [S7][S10]. The budget cited ($1,800) falls within the typical brand-identity range [S27][S28][S29][S30], but the overpayment to $3,200 and the urgency pressure ('reply today') are hallmarks of the scam script.

key_findings.text: Fake-check overpayment scheme: sender offers to mail a $3,200 cheque and asks the recipient to send $1,400 to a vendor via Zelle.
Sender uses a free outlook.com email address while claiming to represent a design studio.
No evidence that 'Quillmere Design Studio' exists as a real company; similar names exist but not this one.
David Laurent's public profiles do not show any affiliation with Quillmere Design Studio or a project manager role there.
The quoted project budget ($1,800) is plausible for a brand identity package, but the overpayment to $3,200 is the trap.

do_not: Do not reply to the message.
Do not provide your phone number or any personal details.
Do not deposit any cheque from this sender.
Do not send money via Zelle or any other method to a 'vendor' or anyone else at their direction.
judgement.next_step: Delete the email and, if desired, report it as phishing/fraud to your email provider or a relevant reporting service.
verification_questions: If this were legitimate, the sender could provide a company-domain email address (e.g., @quillmeredesignstudio.com) and a verifiable company website with a careers or contact page listing this role.
judgement.limitations: The search did not find any official website or business registration for 'Quillmere Design Studio'; however, absence from indexed sources does not absolutely prove non-existence. The assessment relies on the pattern of the message matching known fraud scripts and the lack of corroborating evidence for the claimed identity.

challenge.counter_hypothesis: The message could be legitimate if Quillmere Design Studio is a newly established or small business using a temporary Outlook email for project-specific communication, and the overpayment scenario reflects a genuine vendor reimbursement process rather than a scam.
searches: Quillmere Design Studio LinkedIn company page
David Laurent Quillmere Design Studio Behance or portfolio mention
challenge.strongest_counterpoint: The counter-hypothesis suggests Quillmere Design Studio might be a new/small business legitimately using Outlook for project comms and processing vendor reimbursements via Zelle, though no evidence confirms this.
alternative_explanations: Quillmere Design Studio is a recently registered sole proprietorship using Outlook temporarily while setting up professional infrastructure, and the vendor reimbursement via Zelle reflects a legitimate workflow where the studio fronts costs for trusted partners.

would_change.if: Official business registration records confirm Quillmere Design Studio exists as a legal entity in a jurisdiction matching the sender's claimed location.
would_change.check: Search government business registries (e.g., SEC EDGAR for US, Companies House for UK, or equivalent state/corporate registry) for 'Quillmere Design Studio'.

would_change.if: The sender provides a verifiable landline or professional email domain (e.g., @quillmerestudio.com) linked to the business through independent sources like the company website or regulatory filings.
would_change.check: Look for a professional website associated with Quillmere Design Studio that lists contact details matching the sender's claims, or check domain registration records for a corporate domain.

unresolved: Whether Quillmere Design Studio is a real but obscure business that simply lacks significant online footprint beyond the evidence already examined.

brief.tldr: Do not reply or share personal details; delete the email and report it as phishing.

Claim checks for the company, the recruiter's role, and the payment details are all inconclusive [C1][C2][C3][C4]. The named recruiter, David Laurent, appears in public profiles as an exteriors color specialist, a set designer/photographer in Luxembourg, a recruiter in Arkansas, and a musician — none matching a project manager at Quillmere Design Studio [S17][S18][S19][S20][S21]. Recruitment fraud advisories describe this exact overpayment-and-forward scheme as a known scam [S7][S10]. The budget cited ($1,800) falls within the typical brand-identity range [S27][S28][S29][S30], but the overpayment to $3,200 and the urgency pressure ('reply today') are hallmarks of the scam script.

Sender uses a free outlook.com email address while claiming to represent a design studio.
No evidence that 'Quillmere Design Studio' exists as a real company; similar names exist but not this one.
David Laurent's public profiles do not show any affiliation with Quillmere Design Studio or a project manager role there.
The quoted project budget ($1,800) is plausible for a brand identity package, but the overpayment to $3,200 is the trap.

do_not: Do not reply to the message.
Do not provide your phone number or any personal details.
Do not deposit any cheque from this sender.
Do not send money via Zelle or any other method to a 'vendor' or anyone else at their direction.

judgement.limitations: The search did not find any official website or business registration for 'Quillmere Design Studio'; however, absence from indexed sources does not absolutely prove non-existence. The assessment relies on the pattern of the message matching known fraud scripts and the lack of corroborating evidence for the claimed identity.
